_meta.title: Ritucharya — Ayurvedic Seasonal Dietary & Lifestyle Regimens
_meta.description: Complete seasonal regimen (Ritucharya) defining the six Ayurvedic seasons, their effects on doshas and Agni, and specific dietary/lifestyle recommendations for each. The year is divided into two Ayanas: Uttarayana (Adana Kala - depleting period, sun moves north) and Dakshinayana (Visarga Kala - nourishing period, sun moves south).
_meta.primary_source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra Sthana, Chapter 6 (Tasyashitiya Adhyaya)
_meta.how_to_edit: Each season is independent. To adjust season-to-month mapping for a different region, edit the 'months' and 'approximate_gregorian' fields. Indian subcontinent mapping is default.

uttarayana.description: Sun moves northward. Increasingly hot and dry. Depletes body strength progressively. Fire and wind elements dominant.
uttarayana.body_strength: Progressively decreases from moderate to low
uttarayana.general_principle: Favor nourishing, building foods as the period progresses. Avoid excessive exertion.

dakshinayana.description: Sun moves southward. Moon is powerful. Cool and moist. Builds body strength progressively. Water and earth elements dominant.
dakshinayana.body_strength: Progressively increases from low to high
dakshinayana.general_principle: Body naturally rebuilds. Favor appropriate tastes per season. Strength peaks in Hemanta.

lifestyle_recommendations: Oil massage (Abhyanga) with sesame or mustard oil
Exercise is well-tolerated in this season
Keep body warm, wear warm clothes
Sunbathing (Atapa Sevana) is beneficial
Steam bath after oil massage
shishira.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 6.9-14; Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 3.1-6

vasanta.agni_strength: Variable / can be impaired by Kapha

recommended_foods: Old/aged wheat and rice (at least one year old)
Honey (unheated) — best sweetener for Kapha season
Bitter vegetables: bitter gourd, neem flowers, drumstick
Light meat soups with pepper (for non-vegetarians)

lifestyle_recommendations: Vigorous exercise is strongly recommended
Dry powder massage (Udvartana) to reduce Kapha
Nasya (nasal oil therapy) to clear sinuses
Therapeutic vomiting (Vamana) for Kapha-dominant people
Avoid daytime sleeping
Gargling with warm water and turmeric
vasanta.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 6.22-28; Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 3.18-26

grishma.agni_strength: Weakest of all seasons (body's energy is depleted by heat)

recommended_foods: Rice (especially Shali rice or aged basmati)
Sweet fruits: grapes, mango, coconut, pomegranate, watermelon
Liquid diets: buttermilk, thin soups, rice gruels
avoid_foods: Sour and salty foods in excess
Alcohol or only in very diluted form

lifestyle_recommendations: Stay in cool places, gardens, near water bodies
Apply cooling sandalwood paste on body
Wear light, cotton clothing
Daytime sleep is permitted (only season where it's allowed)
Moonlight walks in the evening
Reduce exercise intensity
Apply cooling oils (coconut, sandalwood)
grishma.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 6.29-34; Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 3.27-37

dosha_state.kapha: Normal but can be triggered by humidity

varsha.agni_strength: Very weak (weakest Agni of the year — most critical season for digestion)
varsha.body_strength: Low (depleted from summer, Vata aggravated by wind and dampness)

recommended_foods: Old/aged grains (especially barley, old rice, old wheat)
Light, warm, freshly cooked food ONLY
Moong dal — lightest of all dals
Soups with ginger, pepper, and cumin
Ghee with meals to support Agni
Medicated water (boiled with ginger, cumin, or coriander)
Thin buttermilk with cumin and rock salt
avoid_foods: Stale or leftover food (contamination risk highest)
Leafy greens (high contamination and worm risk in monsoon)
beverages: Boiled and cooled water with ginger

lifestyle_recommendations: Use boiled water for all purposes
Maintain strict food hygiene
Oil massage followed by warm bath
Fumigation of living spaces with neem/guggulu
Avoid daytime sleep
Avoid excessive exercise
Medicated Basti (therapeutic enema) for Vata pacification
Wear dry, clean clothes; avoid dampness
varsha.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 6.35-40; Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 3.38-48

sharad.dominant_element: Transition: heat returns after rains, clear skies

dosha_state.pitta: Aggravated (Prakopa) — primary concern (sun's heat returns after rains)

recommended_foods: Amla (Indian gooseberry) — best food for this season

lifestyle_recommendations: Virechana (therapeutic purgation) strongly recommended for Pitta
Moonlight exposure is highly beneficial (Sharad moonlight is considered healing)
Apply sandalwood and camphor on body
Wear pearls and light gemstones (cooling effect)
Moderate exercise
Blood-letting for Pitta-dominant individuals (traditional practice)
sharad.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 6.41-48; Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 3.49-58

dosha_state.vata: Can be aggravated by cold (manage with warm foods)
dosha_state.kapha: Accumulating (Sanchaya) — builds up during cold weather

hemanta.agni_strength: Strongest of all seasons (cold contracts body surface, driving Agni inward and intensifying it)

recommended_foods: Rich, heavy, nourishing foods — Agni is strong enough to digest them
avoid_foods: Fasting (strong Agni will consume body tissues if not fed)
beverages: Warm milk (with saffron, turmeric, or cardamom)

lifestyle_recommendations: Daily oil massage (Abhyanga) with warm sesame oil
Vigorous exercise is well-tolerated and recommended
Sunbathing
Warm baths
Wear warm, heavy clothing
Sexual activity is well-tolerated (Shukra Dhatu is strong)
This is the best season for Rasayana (rejuvenation therapy)
hemanta.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 6.9-14; Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 3.1-6

season_mapping._description: Map common English season names and month numbers to Ayurvedic Ritus. This helps the Query Router translate user input (e.g., 'winter') into the correct Ritucharya.
